deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes belong to the 1982 'Champs' manuscripts, which precede Pursuing Stacks (1983). Grothendieck works in a topos (or a more general category) A. He fixes an 'interval' I with a point e -> I, a class C of cofibrations (presumably monomorphisms), and a class W of weak equivalences. Trivial cofibrations (TC) are generated by maps h(i_0, I, e) attached to cofibrations i_0: A_0 -> B_0. On this page h(i_0, I, e) is the map (B_0 x e) ∪ (A_0 x I) -> B_0 x I. In modern terms this is the pushout-product (Leibniz product) i_0 □ (e -> I).

The diagram. The diagram computes, for a second cofibration i': A' -> B', the box product of i' with h(i_0, I, e). The top row joins the pieces ((A' x B_0) x e) ∪ (A' x A_0 x I) and ((B' x B_0) x e) ∪ ((B' x A_0) x I). The vertical maps are h(i_0 x id_{A'}, I, e) and h(i_0 x id_{B'}, I, e). The bottom row is the inclusion A' x B_0 x I -> B' x B_0 x I.

The formula. He finds i' ⊠ h(i_0, I, e) = h(i' ⊠ i_0, I, e). This is the associativity of the pushout-product: i' □ (i_0 □ (e -> I)) ≅ (i' □ i_0) □ (e -> I). He adds that one should also verify the symmetric formula, 'donc on conclut'. The intended conclusion is presumably that C ⊠ TC ⊂ TC, i.e. the generating anodyne maps are stable under pushout-product with cofibrations. This is the key step for a cartesian (SM7-type) closed model structure on the topos.

What is still open. He then lists what is not yet established:
- M1, factorization f = p i in both ways (C, TF) and (TC, F). He says it follows from the 'usual argument', i.e. Quillen's small object argument, using a small generating set of A and filtered colimits. He suggests the lifting properties could be axiomatized via operators L^*, L_* (left/right lifting-orthogonal classes) in a topos or more general category, but postpones this ('to work out' in the margin) and assumes both factorizations.
- M5, saturation of W~. Here W~ is presumably the class of weak equivalences determined by the generated structure.

The goal. He wants to identify W~ with the given W. For that, TC must be made to depend on W: take as the 'bunch' of intervals all intervals I that are W-aspheric over e. He immediately flags the problem: this huge class may make difficulties for the factorization (small object argument).

In short, the page sketches the construction of a cartesian closed model structure on a topos with monomorphisms as cofibrations, anodyne maps generated by an interval, and weak equivalences a prescribed localizer W.
errors: No mathematical error. The associativity of the pushout-product holds in any category where products distribute over pushouts (e.g. any topos), so the formula is correct.
Gap, acknowledged by Grothendieck: the factorization M1 and the saturation M5 are assumed, not proved.

Gap, acknowledged: taking all W-aspheric intervals gives a non-small generating class, so the small object argument does not apply directly. He notes this himself ('may make difficulties for factorisation').
The 'symmetric formula' is only asserted to need checking; it is not written out.

ideas.what: Associativity of the box/pushout-product with the interval map: i' ⊠ h(i_0, I, e) = h(i' ⊠ i_0, I, e), giving stability of anodyne maps under pushout-product with cofibrations
ideas.modern_name: Pushout-product (Leibniz) associativity; anodyne extensions closed under □ with monomorphisms (cartesian model structure / SM7)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gabriel–Zisman (1967) for simplicial anodyne extensions; Cisinski (2002/2006) for general presheaf toposes with an interval
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses intervals and homotopy structures; this exact formula is unsure

ideas.what: Closed model structure on a topos: cofibrations are monos, trivial cofibrations generated by an interval (e, I), factorizations via the small object argument using a small generating set and filtered colimits
ideas.modern_name: Cisinski model structure on a (pre)sheaf topos from an exact cylinder / separating interval
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cisinski (Astérisque 308, 2006); related work by Joyal (1984 letter to Grothendieck) and Jardine (1987) on simplicial (pre)sheaves
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (1983) has related 'modelizer' and model-category discussions

ideas.what: Abstract axiomatization of lifting properties via operators L^*, L_* (left/right orthogonal classes) in a topos or general category
ideas.modern_name: Weak factorization systems; lifting-orthogonality Galois connection (llp/rlp)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen (1967); Bousfield (1977); Adámek–Herrlich–Rosický–Tholen (2002) for weak factorization systems

ideas.what: Make TC depend on W by taking as generating 'bunch' all intervals that are W-aspheric over e, aiming at W~ = W
ideas.modern_name: Model structure determined by a localizer W (Cisinski's W-cofibrant generation, 'smallest localizer' theory)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cisinski (2002–2006), building on Grothendieck's localizers in Pursuing Stacks / Les Dérivateurs
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks treats asphericity relative to localizers, but not this model-structure construction explicitly

missed.claim: In 1982, before Joyal's 1984 letter and Pursuing Stacks, Grothendieck was already trying to build a closed model structure on a general topos. Cofibrations are monos, trivial cofibrations come from interval pushout-products, and the target is W~ = W for a given W. He explicitly identifies the obstacle: a non-small class of W-aspheric intervals versus the small object argument. That obstacle was later resolved by accessibility / Jeff Smith's recognition theorem and by Cisinski's theory.
missed.quote: taking as "bunch" of all intervals I which are W-aspheric over e. But this may make difficulties for factorisation
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's priority for the program later carried out by Cisinski, and pinpoints the exact technical issue (smallness / accessibility) he left open.

missed.claim: Lifting properties are to be axiomatized abstractly via L^*, L_* 'in a topos or a more general category', i.e. a general factorization-system framework for model structures.
missed.quote: The lifting property may again be axiomatized in terms of L^*, L_*, in a topos or a more general category
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early germ of the abstract weak-factorization-system viewpoint. It is modest, as Quillen had the essentials.

deep.surprise_reason: The algebra on the page (pushout-product associativity) is routine. The notable part is the 1982 dating: a clear plan for interval-generated, W-dependent model structures on toposes, with the smallness obstacle correctly flagged. This anticipates Cisinski's work and predates Joyal/Jardine. It is consistent with what is already known about Grothendieck's ideas in Pursuing Stacks, so it is not genuinely surprising.
transcription_corrections: 'vérifiées aussi' should probably read 'vérifier aussi' (i.e. 'also verify the symmetric formula, hence one concludes').

The last lines should read: '...make clear how the definition of (TC) depends on W, taking as "bunch" over e all intervals I which are W-aspheric[?] over e'. The phrase 'over e' is written under '"bunch" of'.
The bottom-left of the diagram is (A' x B_0) x I, with the bottom horizontal arrow an inclusion into B' x B_0 x I.
Labels on the vertical arrows: h(i_0 x id_{A'}, I, e) and h(i_0 x id_{B'}, I, e).
